overview: Suchomimus tenerensis was a huge spinosaurid from the Early Cretaceous Sahara, with a skull shaped almost exactly like a modern gharial — long, narrow and packed with over 100 interlocking conical teeth suited to gripping fish. A low but distinct neural-spine sail ran along its back. Paul Sereno's team discovered it in Niger's Elrhaz Formation in 1997.

As a close relative of Baryonyx, Suchomimus shares the same fish-specialist bauplan: a long narrow snout, large thumb claw and robust forelimbs. It shared its river-delta world with Nigersaurus, the giant crocodilian Sarcosuchus and a diverse fish fauna in what is now the central Sahara.

fossilSites.name: Elrhaz Formation — Gadoufaoua
fossilSites.note: Early Cretaceous fluvial deposits preserving Suchomimus alongside Nigersaurus, Sarcosuchus and abundant fish fauna.

articles.title: Discovery
articles.body: Paul Sereno and colleagues described Suchomimus in 1998 from a partial skeleton including skull material, forelimbs and much of the axial skeleton. Discovery in Niger's Tenere Desert was part of Sereno's decade-long series of major Saharan dinosaur expeditions.

articles.title: Anatomy
articles.body: The gharial-like skull bore teeth with slightly oval cross-section rather than circular — unlike the fully round teeth of Spinosaurus. The thumb claw was large and recurved. A low neural-spine sail was smaller than Spinosaurus's but clearly present. Forelimbs were robust, consistent with fish-snatching behaviour.

articles.title: Ecology
articles.body: The Elrhaz Formation records a vast river delta environment 125–112 Ma. Suchomimus was the apex piscivore in an ecosystem that also included large theropods and the world's largest known crocodyliform, Sarcosuchus imperator, at up to 10 m long.

fossilRecord.paleo: Early Cretaceous African river and floodplain settings.
fossilRecord.evidence: Long jaws, conical teeth and large claw support spinosaurid fish-eating adaptations.

presentation.heroLead: A long-snouted, huge-clawed spinosaurid from the Early Cretaceous of the Sahara, known from a partial skeleton that shows the body plan of the fish-eating theropods better than almost any other.

animalParagraphs: Suchomimus was a large predatory dinosaur from what is now the Ténéré Desert of Niger, described in 1998 from bones collected at Gadoufaoua in the Elrhaz Formation. The main skeleton belonged to an animal roughly ten metres long that was not fully grown; published body masses range from about two and a half to more than five tonnes, and none is well constrained.

Its most striking feature is the skull: a very long, narrow snout with a bulbous tip, an upward-kinked jaw line and dozens of conical, finely serrated teeth, all of which suit gripping slippery prey rather than slicing flesh. The forelimbs were powerful, with an enlarged sickle-shaped claw on the thumb, and tall neural spines along the back and hips formed a low ridge or sail.

Suchomimus belongs to Baryonychinae, the branch of Spinosauridae that also includes Baryonyx from England. Its anatomy is so close to Baryonyx that some researchers have questioned whether the two are distinct genera, and it may also be the same animal as Cristatusaurus, named from fragmentary jaws from the same region.
animalHighlights: A crocodile-like snout more than a metre long with conical teeth and a rosette of enlarged teeth at the tip.
A large, strongly curved claw on the thumb and robust forelimb bones.
Tall neural spines over the back and hips, forming a low ridge rather than the tall sail of Spinosaurus.

lifeCards.label: Feeding
lifeCards.reason: Conical teeth, a narrow snout and enlarged thumb claws match the piscivorous toolkit of Baryonyx, which preserved fish scales. No gut contents are known for Suchomimus itself.

lifeCards.label: Movement
lifeCards.reason: Hindlimb and pelvic bones support two-legged walking. Whether it swam or waded regularly is debated; the evidence from bone density and limb proportions is contested.

lifeCards.label: Known size
lifeCards.reason: Length is scaled from a disarticulated, not fully grown individual. A fixed 5,000 kg mass is not supported; estimates span a wide range.

lifeCards.label: Appearance
lifeCards.reason: The snout, spine ridge and claws are real. Skin, any soft crest, and colour are inferred.

whereFacts.label: Type locality
whereFacts.value: Gadoufaoua, Ténéré Desert, Agadez Region, Niger

locality.name: Gadoufaoua
locality.note: Elrhaz Formation. The type material was collected in 1997 from a single locality in a fossil-rich belt that also yielded Nigersaurus, Ouranosaurus and the giant crocodyliform Sarcosuchus.

presentation.classificationSummary: Suchomimus is a baryonychine spinosaurid, a tetanuran theropod closely related to Baryonyx. Some analyses place the two so close together that they may represent a single genus; its relationship to the poorly known Cristatusaurus from the same rocks is also unresolved.

related.reason: Compare with the closely related English spinosaurid that preserves fish scales as gut contents.
Compare with the tall-sailed, more aquatically adapted spinosaurid from later in the Cretaceous.
Compare with a Brazilian spinosaurid known mainly from a skull.

questions.title: Is it the same as Cristatusaurus or Baryonyx?
questions.copy: Cristatusaurus was named from jaw fragments from the same formation, and Suchomimus differs from Baryonyx only in a few features. Whether either name should be merged is still argued.

questions.title: How heavy was it?
questions.copy: Estimates run from about 2.5 to over 5 tonnes. The skeleton is disarticulated and immature, so no single figure is reliable.

questions.title: Did it hunt in the water?
questions.copy: Its anatomy suits catching fish from the shoreline, but recent analyses disagree on whether spinosaurids like Suchomimus were regular swimmers or wading generalists.

review.ageReviewNote: The Elrhaz Formation is generally correlated to about 115-112 Ma around the Aptian-Albian transition; a 125 Ma lower bound is too old.

specimens.name: Holotype
specimens.note: Disarticulated partial skeleton of a subadult from Gadoufaoua, Elrhaz Formation.

specimens.name: Referred snout
specimens.note: Premaxillae and maxillae forming the front of the snout, from the type locality.

panel.headline: One disarticulated partial skeleton with a referred snout.
panel.standfirst: Suchomimus tenerensis is known chiefly from the holotype, a partial skeleton excavated at Gadoufaoua in 1997, supplemented by a referred snout and other skull pieces from the same locality. Together they cover much of the animal, but no single individual is complete or articulated.

coverage.label: Moderate
coverage.basis: Most skeletal regions are represented across the holotype and referred material, but the skull is incomplete, the bones were disarticulated and most come from one immature individual.

knownRemains.title: What is actually preserved?
knownRemains.summary: The holotype includes parts of the braincase and jaws, cervical, dorsal, sacral and caudal vertebrae with tall neural spines, ribs, the pectoral girdle, forelimbs with the enlarged thumb claw, pelvis and hindlimb bones. A referred specimen preserves the front of the snout.
knownRemains.note: The published estimate of about two thirds of the skeleton refers to the holotype as a whole; its bones were scattered, so their association is taphonomic rather than articulated.

materialGroups.label: Skull and jaws
materialGroups.value: Referred snout with premaxillae and maxillae; braincase, quadrate and partial lower jaw elements with conical teeth. No complete skull.

materialGroups.label: Vertebral column
materialGroups.value: Cervical, dorsal, sacral and caudal vertebrae, including tall-spined dorsals and sacrals, with ribs.

materialGroups.label: Girdles and limbs
materialGroups.value: Scapulocoracoid, robust humerus, radius and ulna, hand with the enlarged thumb claw, pelvis, femur and other hindlimb bones.

materialGroups.label: Exceptional preservation
materialGroups.value: None. No skin, gut contents or soft tissues are known.

interpretation.label: Directly observed
interpretation.value: A partial subadult skeleton with tall neural spines and enlarged thumb claws, plus a referred long, narrow snout with conical teeth.

interpretation.label: Scientific interpretation
interpretation.value: A baryonychine spinosaurid whose jaws and claws suit catching fish and other prey along river margins, with a low sail along the back.

interpretation.label: Still unknown
interpretation.value: Adult size and mass, the full skull, whether it is distinct from Cristatusaurus or Baryonyx, and how much time it spent in water.
